title: Macaroni Cheese
subtitle: Baked pasta in a rich Cheddar and mustard béchamel
excerpt: Short pasta baked in a thick, tangy Cheddar sauce with a crisp breadcrumb crust. The béchamel is made with a generous measure of strong Cheddar and a hit of mustard that keeps the whole thing from being cloying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Macaroni cheese has roots going back to 14th-century Italian and English manuscript cookbooks, but the modern British version is a béchamel-based baked dish that became embedded in home cooking during the 20th century. Thomas Jefferson is often credited with introducing macaroni and cheese to America after seeing it in France, though the dish already existed in American and European cookbooks. The combination of strong Cheddar and English mustard is distinctly British and gives the dish its characteristic sharpness.

content.text: Undercook the pasta slightly before it goes into the sauce. It will finish cooking in the oven and absorb liquid from the béchamel as it bakes: if you cook it to done before baking, it will be overcooked by the time the dish comes out. The béchamel needs to be well seasoned at the sauce stage since it will taste blander once the pasta is incorporated. A good hit of English mustard and a little cayenne are the key to a béchamel that does not taste flat.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions. Drain and set aside.

Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste. Remove from the heat and gradually whisk in the milk, a little at a time, until smooth. Return to a medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, for 8 to 10 minutes until thick and smooth. Season with salt and white pepper.
Remove from the heat. Add the Cheddar, half the Parmesan, the mustard, and cayenne. Stir until the cheese has melted. Add the pasta and stir well. Transfer to a baking dish.
Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Mix the breadcrumbs with the remaining Parmesan and scatter over the top. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.
